table_metadata.table_title: Table 9.1.6: Suggested Schedule of Events-Prophylactic Corticosteroids
table_metadata.table_purpose: Suggested prophylactic corticosteroid course with associated monitoring
table_metadata.notes: Classification (open, D2): typed main_soa because the corticosteroid course applies to every participant (study given prophylactic corticosteroids per design) and runs on its own week grid (D1, Weeks 1-23, 32) concurrent with the post-infusion follow-up; the alternative is subsidiary, since footnote a calls it an example course and its FVIII / liver / hepatitis tests are also reflected in the main Schedule of Events. Footnote a has a printed marker that appears nowhere in the table; it is bound table-wide (schedule_property row 1, synthesized). Dose cells print value and unit on two lines (e.g. "40" / "mg"), joined as "40 mg".

schedule_properties.property_comment: Top header band: "Corticosteroid Treatment Period" (footnote b) spanning columns 2-21 and "Post-Corticosteroid Period" (footnote c) spanning columns 22-26 - periods of the corticosteroid regimen (they run alongside the post-infusion follow-up, so period rather than epoch). Label cell empty, name synthesised.

Unit band printing "Week" once over columns 3-21 and once over columns 22-26; column 2 is covered by the D1 header cell (spans rows 2-3, recorded on row 3). The band only states the unit of the row below and does not tell columns apart: hierarchical_level null. Second synthesised week row in the table, so numbered (§3).

Column labels: D1 (dosing day, single-column label kept as a value of the band) then weeks 1-23 and 32. Week numbers -> week. The label cell prints the activity-column heading "Assessment", so the name is synthesised and numbered as the second week row.

annotations.annotation_text: This table provides an example of a prophylactic corticosteroid course. Clinical judgment, weighing the potential risks and benefits of corticosteroid treatment, should always be exercised when considering adjustment of corticosteroid doses, and discussions between the Investigator and Medical Monitor are advised for any questions or concerns. Dosages are for prednisone or an equivalent dose of another corticosteroid. FVIII and liver tests are also reflected in the Schedule of Events for the study.

Following initiation or completion of corticosteroid regimen, if a recurrence of ALT values > ULN or ≥ 1.5x baseline value is reported, corticosteroid management decisions will be based on discussions between the Investigator and Medical Monitor. Modification of the corticosteroid regimen may take into consideration timing of ALT elevation (prior to or after Week 52), as well as possible confounders for the ALT elevation and adverse events related to corticosteroid dosing. Guidance for tapering oral corticosteroid dosing can be found in Section 9.4.8.2, although a discussion between the PI and Medical Monitor should take place prior to tapering the corticosteroid dose.
After discontinuation of oral corticosteroids, weekly labs for ALT levels and FVIII activity will be measured once a week for 4 weeks to ensure stability in values.
Should only be performed in subjects with a history of hepatitis B or hepatitis C prior to study entry. Tests are also reflected in the Schedule of Events for the study.

review_items.call_made: Table 9.1.6 is typed main_soa: the prophylactic corticosteroid course is given to every participant (the study design includes prophylactic corticosteroids) on its own week grid from infusion Day 1, so it is treated as a schedule every participant passes through.
review_items.alternative: Type it subsidiary: a "suggested" example regimen (footnote a) on a separate week grid whose test rows (FVIII, liver tests, hepatitis tests) are already scheduled in Tables 9.1.2-9.1.4, i.e. supporting detail linked to the main schedule.
